Situation: Your CEO tweeted "our croissants beat therapy" at 3 a.m.
A_Choice: Post a formal apology on LinkedIn
A_Reaction: Nobody asked for an apology. Now everyone is confused.
B_Reaction: Too late: 40 screenshots are already circulating.
C_Choice: Turn it into a campaign: #CroissantTherapy
C_Reaction: The hashtag trends all morning!

Situation: A delivery drone drops a croissant on a famous food critic's head.
A_Reaction: The video reaches 3 million views. You are the villain.
B_Choice: Send her a free box every week for a year
B_Reaction: She writes: "Assault by pastry, but delicious."
C_Choice: Claim it was a "surprise tasting"
C_Reaction: The internet does not buy it.

Situation: A cat influencer with 2 million followers wants to review your croissants.
A_Reaction: The owner posts a sad video. Cat lovers are furious.
B_Reaction: The cat licks one croissant. Sales explode.
C_Choice: Send free croissants, no fee
C_Reaction: The cat sniffs the box and leaves. Polite success.

Situation: Your AI-generated ad shows a hand with six fingers holding a croissant.
A_Choice: Say nothing and hope nobody counts
A_Reaction: Everybody counts. Memes everywhere.
B_Choice: Pull the ad and redo it
B_Reaction: Safe, clean, expensive.
C_Choice: Lean into it: "Six fingers, twice the croissants"
C_Reaction: People love brands that laugh at themselves.

Situation: A 1-star review: "My croissant arrived by drone. I wanted it by hand."
A_Choice: Explain that drones are the future
A_Reaction: You sound like a robot. A grumpy one.
B_Reaction: Your reply gets more likes than the review.
C_Choice: Offer a refund
C_Reaction: The customer is happy, nobody else notices.

Situation: Competitor Baguette Bullet launches drones twice as fast as yours.
A_Choice: Film your bakers at 4 a.m.: quality over speed
A_Reaction: The video is beautiful. Butter, flour, sunrise.
B_Choice: Start a price war: -30% on everything
B_Reaction: Customers love it. Your accountant cries.
C_Choice: Make an ad mocking their drones
C_Reaction: People find it petty.

Situation: Black Friday is coming.
A_Choice: Skip it: "we bake, we don't discount"
A_Reaction: A few people respect that. Quietly.
B_Reaction: Orders explode, quality drops, reviews too.
C_Choice: A limited-edition golden box
C_Reaction: Sold out in two hours.

Situation: A TikTok trend: people try to catch your croissants mid-air from the drones.
A_Reaction: TikTok does not even reply. Everyone else laughs.
B_Reaction: Best catch wins a year of croissants. Huge buzz.
C_Choice: Post a safety warning
C_Reaction: Responsible. Slightly boring.

Situation: A data breach: 5,000 customer addresses have leaked.
A_Choice: Notify everyone, fix it, and offer a free croissant
A_Reaction: The best apology is warm and buttery.
B_Reaction: Journalists disagree. Loudly.
C_Choice: Notify everyone and fix your security
C_Reaction: Painful, but people trust you a bit more.

Situation: An intern posts a meme on the official account by mistake. 300,000 likes.
A_Reaction: Mysterious. It works, sort of.
B_Reaction: Fans want the meme back.
C_Choice: Promote the intern to Chief Meme Officer
C_Reaction: The intern is now more famous than your CEO.

Situation: A celebrity is photographed eating one of your croissants.
A_Reaction: Clever and cheap. Marketing at its best.
B_Reaction: Some people notice. Nice.
C_Choice: Offer a sponsorship deal
C_Reaction: Expensive, but your logo is now on prime time TV.

Situation: Drone battery failure: 200 Sunday orders lost.
A_Reaction: The others complain about that too.
B_Reaction: It was sunny. Everyone checked.
C_Choice: Refund everyone and post an apology video
C_Reaction: Honest, human, appreciated.

Situation: Your Google Ads campaign has a 0.3% CTR and is burning cash.
A_Choice: Move the budget to Instagram Stories
A_Reaction: Croissants look better in vertical video.
B_Choice: Double the budget, it will pick up
B_Reaction: It did not pick up.
C_Choice: Pause it and rewrite the ads
C_Reaction: Better ads, smaller bill.

Situation: A newspaper asks: are drone-delivered croissants bad for the planet?
A_Choice: Run an ad full of trees and sunsets
A_Reaction: Greenwashing detected in 12 minutes.
B_Reaction: The headline writes itself.
C_Choice: Publish your real carbon footprint
C_Reaction: Transparency wins you serious respect.

Situation: A fan draws a croissant-shaped drone. The drawing goes viral.
A_Reaction: You just attacked a fan. Bad idea.
B_Choice: Share it and credit the artist
B_Reaction: The artist is thrilled. So are your fans.
C_Choice: Buy the design to sell T-shirts
C_Reaction: The T-shirts sell out. The artist gets paid.

Situation: A traditional bakery accuses you of killing small bakeries.
A_Reaction: Silence looks like guilt.
B_Reaction: You hold your ground. Nobody really wins.
C_Choice: Partner with local bakeries
C_Reaction: Your drones now deliver their bread too.

Situation: Your newsletter typo: "Fresh croissants, delivered by drunk".
A_Reaction: Some customers are now worried about the pilots.
B_Reaction: Fine. Forgettable.
C_Choice: Follow-up: "Our drones are sober, we promise"
C_Reaction: Best open rate of the year.

Situation: An investor wants you to use cheaper butter.
A_Choice: Test it secretly on one product
A_Reaction: A food blogger finds out. Butter-gate begins.
B_Reaction: Customers taste the difference within a week.
C_Choice: Refuse: "we never touch the butter"
C_Reaction: The investor leaves. Your fans cheer.

Situation: A video shows a pigeon riding one of your drones.
A_Reaction: The pigeon flies away. So does the buzz.
B_Reaction: Captain Pigeon gets his own merch line.
C_Choice: Publish a drone safety statement
C_Reaction: Serious. Responsible. Zero likes.

Situation: An agency offers 50,000 fake followers for 500 EUR.
A_Choice: Report the agency to the platform
A_Reaction: You get a thank-you note and some press.
B_Reaction: A journalist spots the fake accounts.
C_Choice: Decline
C_Reaction: Integrity costs nothing today.

Situation: Valentine's Day is next week.
A_Reaction: Just another Tuesday.
B_Reaction: Couples love them. Instagram loves them more.
C_Choice: Campaign: "Single? Croissants don't judge"
C_Reaction: Singles everywhere feel seen.

Situation: A neighborhood complains about drone noise.
A_Choice: Give every neighbor a free croissant
A_Reaction: Complaints turn into orders.
B_Reaction: Now they complain at 2 a.m.
C_Choice: Upgrade to silent propellers
C_Reaction: Silence is golden. And expensive.

Situation: A LinkedIn guru calls you "the Uber of pastries".
A_Choice: Reply: "We're more the croissant of croissants"
A_Reaction: Nobody understands. Everybody shares.
B_Reaction: Your mum likes the post.
C_Choice: Invite him to visit the bakery
C_Reaction: He posts 14 selfies with flour on his face.

Situation: Your website crashes during a live TV mention.
A_Reaction: Back online. Moment missed.
B_Choice: Blame your host on social media
B_Reaction: Customers don't care whose fault it is.
C_Choice: Put up a "Rocket refueling" page with a promo code
C_Reaction: The waiting page goes viral.

Situation: A customer had an allergic reaction: the allergen is missing from your product page.
A_Reaction: Safe, but customers miss it.
B_Choice: Update the labels and call the customer
B_Reaction: Fast, caring, fixed.
C_Choice: Reply: "read the small print"
C_Reaction: There was no small print. Disaster.

Situation: A comedian posts a parody of your latest ad.
A_Choice: Hire the comedian for your next ad
A_Reaction: The new ad is the funniest of the year.
B_Choice: Ask for it to be removed
B_Reaction: The Streisand effect: now everyone has seen it.
C_Choice: Share it and thank the creator
C_Reaction: Good sport! Your followers love it.

Situation: Supplier delay: no almonds for a week.
A_Choice: Launch a "mystery croissant" of the day
A_Reaction: People love surprises.
B_Choice: Sell plain croissants as almond ones
B_Reaction: Customers notice. Of course they notice.
C_Choice: Announce an "almond-free week" with a discount
C_Reaction: Honest and kind of charming.

Situation: A rival posts fake bad reviews about you.
A_Reaction: You win. Eventually. Expensively.
B_Choice: Post fake good reviews in return
B_Reaction: Now both brands look terrible.
C_Choice: Report them and respond calmly
C_Reaction: The platform removes the fake reviews.

Situation: A radio show wants your CEO live at 6 a.m.
A_Reaction: They invite Baguette Bullet instead.
B_Reaction: He falls asleep live on air.
C_Choice: Send the head baker with fresh croissants
C_Reaction: The hosts eat live. Pure radio gold.

Situation: End of quarter: the board wants growth, now.
A_Reaction: Revenue up, love down.
B_Reaction: Growth, yes. Profit, no.
C_Choice: Referral program: bring a friend, get a croissant
C_Reaction: Customers become your sales team.

Situation: A drone delivers croissants into a classroom during an exam.
A_Reaction: The teacher accepts your apology but gives the drone a zero.
B_Reaction: Students place orders but the university bans your drones.
C_Choice: Create a quiet delivery zone outside the campus
C_Reaction: Students get breakfast and teachers get silence.

Situation: Chinese students ask for a red bean croissant during a campus food festival.
A_Reaction: The croissants sell out before the festival music starts.
B_Choice: Replace every classic croissant without testing
B_Reaction: Regular customers demand the return of their usual breakfast.
C_Choice: Invite students to a tasting session
C_Reaction: Their feedback improves the recipe and makes them feel included.

Situation: Your drone delivers a customer's proposal ring to the wrong picnic.
A_Choice: Arrange an urgent replacement delivery for free
A_Reaction: The ring arrives just in time and the customer says yes to your service.
B_Choice: Tell the customer to find it themselves
B_Reaction: The complaint gets more attention than the proposal.
C_Choice: Refund the delivery and send an apology box
C_Reaction: The customer appreciates the gesture but keeps the drone off the wedding list.
